judged_text: In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a reference's credentialId is absent from this.calendarCredentials and the DB fetch returns nothing (or the app relation/slug is missing), `credential` stays undefined and is passed unguarded to `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))`, unlike the create path which guards with `if (credential)`. One dangling calendar reference (e.g. a deleted credential) aborts the whole update loop into the catch block, returning failure results for ALL calendar references instead of updating the remaining valid ones — a partial-failure amplification that the new DB-fallback branch makes reachable and that no test in the diff triggers.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (renamed/rewritten section around `calendarReference = ...filter(...)`), inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set but no matching credential exists in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup either returns null or lacks `app.slug`, `credential` remains `undefined`, yet the code still does `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` without a guard. This can throw and is caught by the outer `try/catch`, which then returns failure results for *all* calendar references (`calendarReference?.map(...)`), amplifying a single bad/deleted credential into a full failure instead of updating remaining valid references. The create path (`createAllCalendarEvents`) explicitly guards with `if (credential)` before calling `createEvent`, highlighting the inconsistency.
